name: c-portrait-straight-to-camera
prompt: A tall portrait drawing in black ink on warm off-white paper, done like a hand-inked newspaper satire from just after the First World War but plainly our own original character: a stout, heavily jowled plutocrat sits squarely in the middle of a plain slatted wooden park bench, seen dead-on at eye level, full figure from the polished toes of his spats to the crown of a tall silk top hat. He sits wide and settled, gloved hands folded over a round waistcoat stretched across his belly, a watch chain looped across it, a fat cigar tucked in the corner of his mouth, and he looks straight out of the page at the viewer with a small, contented, knowing smile, eyes slightly hooded, entirely at ease. The two empty seats either side of him tell the story: on his left, a wooden crutch lies dropped across the slats; on his right, a hospital lanyard with a blank plastic badge hangs over the edge of the seat. Linework is fine and confident, form built by layered parallel hatching and tight crosshatch in the coat, hat and shadows under the bench, with the face kept clean and clear for reading, simple bold contour around the whole figure. No park scenery behind him at all, just the bare paper with a short ground line and a soft hatched shadow under the bench, even flat light from the front, no dramatic shadows, so he reads like a clean character model sheet. Pure black ink on cream paper, no colour, no tone wash. A wide empty band of untouched paper fills the upper third above the top of his hat. No words, letters, signature, numbers or caption drawn anywhere in the image. Thanks.
